title: Postcarding & Conversation with Jerry Goldfeder, election law and ranked choice voting expert
description:
Join us starting at 9:30am ET to write postcards, talk about the news, and hear from candidates and political leaders. If this is your first time joining this group, please sign on at least 15 minutes before the speaker start time listed below. 

Please answer the registration questions accurately and completely. Also, having your full name displayed will facilitate admission from the waiting room. We may request clarification from you in the waiting room chat. 

**Jerry Goldfeder will join us at 10:00am on Tuesday, June 10.** We welcome Jerry back for "A Crash Course in Ranked Choice Voting." Jerry has had a 40-year career concentrating on election law and voting rights representing candidates for local, state, and federal office, including several candidates for President of the United States. Jerry currently serves as Director of Fordham Law School's Voting Rights and Democracy Project, chairs the New York State Bar Association's Voting Rights and Democracy Task Force, serves on the New York City Bar Association's Rule of Law Task Force, and acts as a special adviser to the American Bar Association's Election Law Committee.  Since 2003, Jerry has taught Election Law at Fordham Law School, and has also taught at the University of Pennsylvania Law School. A prolific writer, he authored the treatise Goldfeder's Modern Election Law, now in its 6th Edition, and has published articles in various academic journals as well as the New York Times, the L.A. Times, USA Today, the New York Daily News, and other publications. Jerry also writes the New York Law Journal column, Election and Political Law.

We strive to build community, educate voters, and use our Sharpies to write to save democracy together. Write postcards with us or just join the conversation. If you need help getting started with postcarding, please visit our [FAQ](https://markersfordemocracy.org/postcarding/postcarding-faq).

If you are with the media and want to attend, you must notify us at markersfordemocracy@gmail.com at least two hours before the start of the event. All discussions are off the record.

This event is co-hosted by [Markers For Democracy](https://markersfordemocracy.org), [Downtown Nasty Women Social Group](https://linktr.ee/DNWSG), and [Team Min](https://linktr.ee/teammin

title: Access Denied: The Growing Threat to Press Freedom in the U.S.
description: Join Sherman Smith, Editor-in-Chief of the Kansas Reflector (a States Newsroom affiliate), for a vital conversation on the growing restrictions facing journalists at both the state and federal levels. From blocked access to legislative chambers in states like Kansas, Texas, and New York, to increasing hurdles at the White House, Sherman will explore how these trends threaten press freedom and public accountability. title: Renewable Energy Action Call
description:
Native voices have the power to influence energy policy in Apache and Navajo counties.  Join us to learn how contacting your county's decision makers can protect our precious water and air.   In the face of drought and climate change it is up to citizens like us to speak out for our planet.  We have more power in local matters than on national policy so raise your voice locally to protect what we care about most.  Our families, our commuites and our lands.  

Navajo and Apache Counties are revising their renewable energy ordinances and need input from community members who want to protect our water and air.  They need to hear why renewables are a better choice than coal and other dirty energy sources.   Learn from our panel of presenters about the impacts of dirty energy on our communities and why large scale renewable energy is safer for our families and our planet.  You will also learn how you can address local decision makers like the County Board of Supervisors and Planning and Zoning Committees to ask for clean energy ordinances that protect our air, water and our history.

title: Join the McLennan County Democratic Party at the Waco Juneteenth Parade
description:
Walk/Ride in the parade!

The McLennan County Democratic Party will have a float in the Waco Juneteenth Parade, Saturday 14 June. We need up to 19 volunteers to sign up to decorate our pickup truck and then ride/walk in the parade. We need 4 volunteers to take turns marching with our banner. The parade Route runs from the Heritage Square staging area, 311 Austin Ave in front of City Hall to the old Campus of Paul Quinn Campus, 820 Elm Street, a nice little walk on a warm and sunny day.

Those walking and riding with the float are encouraged to wear We the People - March for Democracy T-shirts if you have one or Democratic Party or Civil Rights related T-shirts and hats are an important thing to wear.

Sign up on Mobilize!

McLennan County Deputy Voter Registrars Needed for the Parade!

In addition to those volunteering with the float, we need 4, able bodied, McLennan County credentialed Volunteer Deputy Voter Registrars to circulate through the assembly area and then walk the entire parade route registering voters. We always get a few. Smile and walk up to people and ask them if they need to register. These are two, 2 person teams one on each side of the street. Bring your supplies, good shoes and wear hats. The We the People shirt or Neutral Patriotic or Civil rights T-shirts and hats are good for this, nothing that says Democratic Party or promotes a candidate. Lots of walking.
